god_relations.myth: Apollo appears to Bernardo in a dream or vision
god_relations.note: Apollo appears to Bernardo in a dream or vision within Balbuena’s learned epic.
Modern mythography identifies Sugaar with Culebro and makes him Zuria’s father.
Gabriel receives Roland’s soul and carries it to paradise.

Almanzor.note: He coordinates with Ruy and Muslim commanders to destroy the brothers.

Count García Fernández.note: He knights all seven brothers together on one day.
He imposes reconciliation after Gonzalo González and Ruy fight.

Culebro.note: Culebro impregnates Zuria’s Scottish mother during a dream.

Doña Lambra.note: Lambra humiliates Gonzalo González and demands punishment after he kills her servant.

Doña Sancha.note: She is the mother of all seven brothers.

Ferracutus.note: Roland duels the giant for several days and debates Christian doctrine.
Roland exploits the giant’s revealed vulnerability and kills him through the navel.

Froom.note: Later harmonization identifies Zuria with the earlier English royal founder Froom.

Galve.note: The Muslim commander is associated with the battle against the Infantes.

God.note: A heavenly voice prescribes Rodrigo’s penance; God receives him after punishment.

God.myth: God grants fortune and victories to the Cid
God.note: Rodrigo prays to God, who is credited with his fortune and victories.
Fernán prays, and God grants providential success to his campaigns.
God reverses missiles, grants victory, collapses the mountain, and restores the Church.
Roland confesses, raises his glove, and offers himself to God.
God receives Roland and halts the sun for Charlemagne’s vengeance.

Gonzalo Gustioz.note: He is the father of all seven brothers.

Hercules.note: Later legend associates Rodrigo’s forbidden chamber with a structure named for Hercules.

Jesus Christ.myth: Pelayo invokes Christ during his debate with Oppa
Jesus Christ.note: Pelayo invokes Christ as advocate with the Father and source of rescue.

Michael “of the Peril”.note: Michael carries Roland’s soul to paradise with Gabriel and a cherub.

Mudarra González.note: He is their posthumous paternal half-brother and avenger.

Nuño Salido.note: Their foster-father and tutor raises the seven brothers.
He reads ominous birds, warns them, and dies fighting beside them.

Olaf the White.myth: Viking reconstruction of the White Lord
Olaf the White.note: Jon Bilbao proposed Olaf as a historical analogue or identity for Zuria.

Pelayo of Arlanza.note: Pelayo receives Fernán at his hermitage and foretells his victory.
The deceased Pelayo appears in Fernán's dream before the battle.

Ruy Velázquez.note: Their maternal uncle betrays them and coordinates the ambush causing their deaths.
Ruy attacks Gonzalo González, who strikes him with a goshawk.

Saint Gabriel.myth: Gabriel promises the exiled Cid success in a dream
Saint Gabriel.note: Gabriel appears in a dream and promises Rodrigo success.

Saint James.myth: Santiago aids the dead Cid's final victory
Saint James.note: Saint James assists Rodrigo's posthumous mounted sortie against Búcar's forces.
Saint James.source: Estoria de España and Cardeña complex

Saint James.note: James appears mounted with the celestial host and aids Fernán's army.

Saint Lazarus.myth: The disguised Lazarus tests Rodrigo's hospitality
Saint Lazarus.note: Disguised as a leper, Lazarus tests Rodrigo when he shares food or lodging.

Saint Lazarus.myth: Lazarus blesses Rodrigo after the hospitality test
Saint Lazarus.note: After revealing himself, Lazarus rewards Rodrigo's compassion with a blessing.

Saint Millán.note: Millán announces heavenly aid and gives Fernán tactical instructions.
Millán joins the celestial host that secures Fernán's victory.

Saint Peter.note: Fernán patronizes Peter's Arlanza sanctuary and chooses it as his burial place.

Virgin Mary.myth: The Cid invokes Mary in prayer and warfare
Virgin Mary.note: Rodrigo invokes Mary in prayers associated with his Christian victories.
Fernán invokes Mary within the poem's devotional framework, without a distinct apparition.

Virgin Mary.myth: Missiles rebound from Mary’s cave at Covadonga
Virgin Mary.note: Pelayo shelters in Mary’s house, from which the attackers’ missiles rebound.

Virgin Mary.myth: Virgin visibly appears to Pelayo at Covadonga
Virgin Mary.note: Later paintings and devotional accounts depict a personal Marian apparition absent from the early chronicle.

the Devil.myth: The demon tempts the penitent Rodrigo
the Devil.note: A female demon assumes a form associated with Cava to tempt Rodrigo.

Álvar Sánchez.note: Gonzalo González surpasses his rival in the games and kills him.
